about: Brand-neutral default palette for data visualization. Categorical hues follow an established colorblind-safe qualitative set (distinguishable under deuteranopia, protanopia, and tritanopia). Sequential and diverging ramps are perceptually ordered by luminance. Every value is a six-digit hex. To rebrand, replace the accent and categorical values with your own brand hues and RE-CHECK contrast and colorblind separation; keep the neutral theme scaffold (background, panel, gridline, axis, text) unless your brand mandates otherwise. See color.md for the swap procedure and contrast rules.

categorical.note: Ordered by assignment priority. Use in order; do not shuffle per chart. On a light background the final entries (yellow) have weak contrast for thin marks - use them for large fills only. Pick the theme variant that matches the page.

sequential.note: Light-to-dark, low-to-high value. Perceptually ordered by decreasing relative luminance. Use for a single quantitative field with a meaningful zero or floor.

diverging.note: Blue (low) through a neutral midpoint to orange (high). Blue-orange is colorblind-safer than red-green for diverging data. Anchor the neutral midpoint at the meaningful zero, not at the data median.

semantic.note: Reserve these for meaning (good/bad/warn/info), never as decoration. Do not encode a category with a semantic color unless the category IS that meaning. The light set is tuned to read as colored TEXT on a light page; the dark set is lightened so the same meanings read as text on the dark background.
